title: Private CP Day-One Labs and TF Workflows (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft runbook for day‑one on‑prem / VPC installations of the Private Control Plane (Private CP). It focuses on bootstrapping a minimal, production‑intent control plane, Terraform module workflow notes, scaling steps for additional nodes, and rotation/upgrade playbooks. Goal: give field engineers a repeatable, low‑risk path from zero -> healthy cluster and a clear rollback story.

Scope / Audience:
- Audience: field deployment engineers, SREs supporting customer Private CP cutovers, solutions engineering.
- Not covering: customer application onboarding, model packaging, or dedicated GPU pool provisioning (see separate docs).

Quick inventory (pre‑flight):
- Admin laptop (ssh keys with org cert)
- Access to customer KMS / HSM credentials (wrap + rotation policy)
- Terraform service account with project-level permissions and lock on remote state backend
- DNS / IP plan for control plane (api, etcd, loadbalancer, operators)
- Certificate lifetimes & CA signing process (internal CA or ACME)
- BMC / baremetal access or cloud console credentials for node provisioning
- Monitoring endpoints: prometheus, grafana, alerting channels validated

Day‑One bootstrap sequence (minimal, numbered checklist):
1) Confirm preflight inventory (above) and open a deployment ticket in Jira (INF-1427 style). Attach customer contact + SRE oncall.
2) Create a deployment workspace in Terraform: TF_WORKSPACE=customer-<shortname>-cp-day1
   - Lock remote state: terraform init with backend lock; confirm S3/consul/GCS lock acquired.
3) Apply infra primitives only: vpc subnets, route tables, bastion SG, k8s control plane SG.
   - Command: terraform apply -target=module.net -target=module.bastion -var-file=customer.tfvars
   - Note: keep module bootstrap footprint small to reduce blast radius.
4) Provision control plane seed nodes (3) and etcd cluster: ensure anti-affinity across racks/AZs.
5) Validate node-level telemetry (node exporter, journald shipping, disk usage).
6) Apply control plane k8s manifests via the deployment operator (operator initial image pinned).
7) Run smoke tests: /healthz, control plane API latency < 200ms p50, etcd quorum stable, etcd db size within expected range.
8) Register initial operator certificate and validate operator can reconcile (check logs for leader election, TLS handshake).
9) Promote TF workspace to the canonical customer workspace and tag the run: tag=day1-boot-<date>.

Terraform module and workflow notes (pragmatic tips):
- Module boundaries: keep 'network', 'bootstrap', 'controlplane', 'kms' and 'dns' separate. Finer granularity = safer targeted applies and rollbacks.
- Variables: never commit customer secrets in repo. Use vault or encrypted tfvar files in customer repo.
- State locking: always use remote state with locks (DynamoDB/Consul/GCS locks). For airgapped installs, use local Consul in HA mode.
- Workspaces: prefer per‑customer workspace rather than per‑env in the same state to reduce accidental cross‑apply.
- Drift detection: add a nightly tf plan job that runs in read‑only mode and files a ticket if plan != empty.
- Version pinning: pin terraform provider and module versions. Put provider version bump in a dedicated PR and run a canary apply against a staging workspace.
- Example commands: 
  - terraform init -backend-config="bucket=redwood-cp-state" -reconfigure
  - terraform plan -var-file=customer.tfvars -out=plan.tfplan
  - terraform apply "plan.tfplan"
  - terraform state pull > state.json (for offline debugging)

Scaling notes (adding capacity / edge nodes):
- When scaling horizontally, prefer rolling additions rather than batch applies. Add nodes one AZ/rack at a time.
- Autoscaling signals: CPU util, queue depth on inference proxy, and p50 token latency per route. Tune thresholds conservatively for first week.
- Node labels: tag nodes with deploy epoch (e.g., cp-v1-20241003) to allow targeted cordon/drain/rollback.
- Draining: kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data <node>. Wait for pods to reschedule and for application-level tests before proceeding.

Rotation and upgrade playbook (control plane components):
- Prechecks:
  - Confirm backup of etcd (s3:gpg-encrypted) and snapshot restored successfully to a staging env in the last 7 days.
  - Run smoke test harness (smoke-suite v2) and record baseline metrics.
- Canary upgrade flow:
  1) Build new operator/controlplane images and push to customer registry.
  2) Deploy to canary node pool (1 node in non-critical AZ).
  3) Run full smoke-suite + e2e: API responses, leader election, cert rotation, webhook behaviors.
  4) If canary OK for 30m, rollout to next pool.
- Rolling restarts: use orchestration tool (kubectl rollout restart or operator hooks) with maxUnavailable=1 for controlplane statefulsets.
- Risk mitigation: keep a warm fallback controlplane image tag pinned (e.g., stable-20240930) and a documented rollback command.
- Rollback command examples: kubectl rollout undo deployment/controlplane-operator --to-revision=<n> and run etcd restore only if quorum compromised.

Emergency evacuations (fast path):
- If control plane API is unresponsive for > 5 minutes and all leader checks fail:
  1) Scale up a fallback pool (preseeded image) via terraform -target=module.fallback_pool apply
  2) Update external LB to point to fallback pool's ELBs (DNS TTLs should be preconfigured to 60s).
  3) Open SOC incident and declare degraded mode.

Validation and post-deploy checks (smoke + thorough):
- Service health endpoints: controlplane/health, operator/health, etcd/health. Should be green.
- Traces: ensure traces appear in tracing backend within 30s of a test request.
- Cost and capacity: check initial token throughput and backpressure behavior (no 5xx on inference proxy).
- Security: confirm KMS access patterns and IAM roles are correct; run a least-privilege scan.

Common pitfalls discovered in field (notes to self):
- IPAM conflicts: customer onprem DHCP ranges sometimes overlap; always verify declared CIDR against inventory spreadsheet before apply.
- Certificate expiration: automatic rotation may fail if CA signing endpoint is blocked; have a manual cert injection path documented.
- TF provider mismatch: provider upgrades have caused apply diffs that changed loadbalancer behavior; always run provider upgrade in staging first.
- Large etcd WALs: if WAL growth observed during bootstrap, reduce logging level on operators temporarily and investigate pending watch loops.

Testing plan (what to assert in the next deploy run):
- Add weighted traffic canary test to the day‑one checklist: route 2% of requests to canary operator for 1h, watch error budget.
- Run inject‑latency tests to ensure autoscaler thresholds don't overreact to brief spikes.

TODOs / follow ups:
- Convert this draft into a compact checklist playbook for the oncall runbook page.
- Author a Terraform linter ruleset for our private modules (for variable naming and tag enforcement).
- Automate nightly drift detection and create PRs against infra repo when safe changes are detected.

Appendix: handy commands & quick snippets
- Check etcd snapshots: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot status /var/lib/etcd/member/snap.db
- Restore etcd (debug): ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot restore snap.db --name restored-cluster --initial-cluster-token tkn
- Quick TF plan for network only: terraform plan -target=module.network -var-file=customer.tfvars
- Drain node: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force

Contact and escalation:
- Primary owner: Asha Patel (ashap@redwood.ai)
- SRE oncall rotation: see /confluence/sre-oncall
- Field deploy lead: Miguel Ortega

Footnotes / references:
- See CONFLUENCE:Private-CP-Operator-Design for higher level architecture notes.
- Keep ticket reference INF-1427 in every deploy PR.

--- End of document.
